questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose my destination based on my personal interest in Arctic Science, and UNIS is the best university offering hands-on insight into the physical geography of a High-Arctic setting as well as specialised Arctic geographic field methods.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been the best educational and social experience I have ever partaken in. UNIS is a highly professional university with dedicated and competent staff, and the remote setting means that everyone get to experince the true Arctic and partake in the local community.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Before arrival all necessary information was sent to me via email, from how to arrive from the airport to the first day at UNIS. From there information was communicated by teachers on a regular basis.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When arriving at the university you enter the reception where you state your name and are handed a letter with all information you need as well as an access card to the university, library, printing etc. and you are directed to your first location, where you receive further information. Simple and easy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: As always, when at a new institution it can be hard to find your way around, so further information about where rooms are located could have been helpful. But you can easily yourself take a walk around the halls and locate the rooms, that are all named, in advance.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Samskipnaden provides all student housing on Svalbard. It is very easy. You go to their website, select the type of room you want, and upload your documentation of admission to UNIS and they send you a contract to sign.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The student housing is newly constructed as of this August and September. The buildings are very nice and have everything you need. Also, they are located in the middle of town close to all you need and less than a 10 min walk from UNIS.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At UNIS it is very easy to register. If going through an exchange programme in Oslo, it is equally simple to register there. You are sent a link, where you register in a department and write that you will be attending UNIS, not Oslo.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You apply for the courses through the UNIS website. UNIS sends you a link with an offer in case of admission, and you confirm if you wish to attend. And that is it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: KU contacted UiO that sent me a link to register in (a formality). You register yourself at UNIS directly through their website and can always contact them via email or phone if help is needed. They respond immediately (so does UiO).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I applied for the classes I wanted, and was lucky to get a place at all of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look through the course catalogue on their website (under studies) and apply for anything you find interesting. UNIS will admit you to all the courses you want if there is space. And then you can choose and accept the courses you want to attend.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: High level of professionalism and content, and extremely dedicated and competent professors. The small locatioin means that you work very closely with them on a high academic level which is very satisfying.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses are very high and hands-on as the university is located in the setting you are studying. I have learned more about physical geography in the six months I was there, than I have the last three years at a theoretical education at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: KU is solely based on theory minus 1-2 courses. UNIS is solely based on field work minus 1-2 courses. It provides you with skills that are highly usefull and sought out in the field of Arctic Science.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AG-204 The Physical Geography of Svalbard
AG-221 Arctic Physical Geographical Field Techniques

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
These two courses are intertwined and are highly recommended to take together. I would highly recommend these two courses (if they still exist) as they provide a profound insight into the entire field of Arctic geographical science.

Besides these, there are plenty of very good master courses with the same type of focus, such as glaciaology and hydrology.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had a hospital bill of about 400.00

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive as everything is shipped there. Alcohol is slightly cheaper than mainland Norway as Svalbard is taxfree. There are a lot of nice sportshops where items are also slightly cheaper than mainland and UNIS students can get discounts there too (10-15%).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UNIS has a stundet council whose job is to provide social opportunities for the rest of the students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The student counsil organised parties, dinners, bonfires, bingo, and other social events. They also arranged a regular night at Svalbard Bryggeri for students with 20% discount every other Saturday.

There are a kayak club, and a local gym where you can exercise, play volleyball, floorball, swim etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking in the area is the best way to see Svalbard. There are endless beautiful hikes to do around town (grab a bunch of people and a riffle and head out into the wilderness) to the mountain plateaus or to Nordenskiöldtoppen (1050 m a.s.l.). Join all the local events: Dark Season Blues Festival (blues festival), Arctic Chamber music festival (classical music), talks in Kulturhuset, the cinema, visit the local bars, waffle and game nights at the church, and visit the dogyards. UNIS also has a student cabin in Bjørndalen that you can borrow which is a really nice valley to visit and where you and your fellow students can have a bonfire and cook dinner together.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Same as above. There are also boat trips to Pyramiden and Barentsburg that are definitely worth a trip.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The town and community are very small and everyone are very nice. Be polite and greet everyone, and your stay will be very pleasent.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: All students are there for a limited time, there are no local students. This also means that everyone partakes in all the social acitivities, so you will get to know everyone. You will have a kitchen where you meet people, and as all students live in the same building, you will eventually meet everyone, maybe at the kitchen-to-kitchen party?

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
I found no such challenges, as everyone you socialise with are new to the area, and therefore act very nice and inclusive to all.
The town is small and quite, so treat it that way.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate the small town and community, and the closeness to wilderness and wildlife, how people live under nature's conditions and not the other way around.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The environment is cold and teaching is based on field work, so bring warm and practical clothes (hiking pants, wind and waterproof jacket and good hiking boots). Remember that you also have to go to class and attend parties, so also bring nice clothes (i forgot this). Take advantage of you time there, and go on as many hikes as you can while there is still daylight.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry too much about the application process through another university, as that will sort out, just make sure that you have an application in with UNIS with the courses you want to apply for. You can find all you need to know about the town, proper clothing, safety etc. at the UNIS website. Your first week at the university is a safety course, where you learn everything you need to know about safety: hiking in the field, travelling by ocean, and polar bear safety, so you need not worry about any of this.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything! The courses were absolutely brilliant, the field work was amazing, the weekend hikes were breathtaking, and the occasional, daily reindeer encounter is just adorable.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Your limitations are moved when you work your way through the wilderness of Svalbard, whether it is crossing a wild river, fearing to fall in, or hiking to the plateaus, and have a fear of heights. Afterwards you feel like you can do anything.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
